lessons.title: বাড়ি গিয়ে খেলাম (bāṛi giye khelām) — one action, then the next
lessons.gloss: I went home and ate — the -e form that joins one action to the next

segments.text: Say "I was reading when Mira came". (jôkhon āmi bôi pôṛchhilām, tôkhon mīrā elô.) Then the word for "please", দয়া করে: "having done a kindness". Its করে is the form of this lesson.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: the -e form

segments.text: আমি স্টেশনে গিয়ে টিকিট কিনলাম। āmi sṭeshône giye ṭikiṭ kinlām. — "I went to the station and bought a ticket."

গিয়ে is যাওয়া in the -e form: "having gone". It finishes one action so the next can start, and the last verb carries the tense for both. Most verbs add -এ to the stem: করা becomes করে (kore), দেখা becomes দেখে (dekhe), বসা becomes বসে (bose). An আ in the stem becomes এ: আসা becomes এসে (ese), নামা becomes নেমে (neme), হাঁটা becomes হেঁটে (hẽṭe). An এ said e, or an ও, rises: কেনা becomes কিনে (kine). The verbs whose stem ends in a vowel take -য়ে: খাওয়া becomes খেয়ে (kheye), নেওয়া becomes নিয়ে (niye), দেওয়া becomes দিয়ে (diye).

The -e form can also say how: হেঁটে গেলাম (hẽṭe gelām), "I went on foot". And it pairs with a second verb that adds a shade rather than a new action: বসে পড়লাম (bose pôṛlām), "I sat down", with পড়া in its other sense, "to fall"; হারিয়ে গেল, "it got lost", which you know.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: one doer

segments.text: Both actions belong to the same person: আমি বাড়ি গিয়ে খেলাম (āmi bāṛi giye khelām), "I went home and ate". When someone else does the second thing, Bengali says two sentences: আমি বাড়ি গেলাম। মীরা খেল।.

lessons.title: প্রথমে … তারপর … শেষে (prôthôme … tārpôr … sheshe) — the order of a story
lessons.gloss: first … after that … in the end — the order of a story

segments.text: Say "I went home and ate". (āmi bāṛi giye khelām.) Then say প্রথমে, "at first", and শেষ, "the end".

blocks.title: You'll want to know: first, then

segments.text: প্রথমে আমরা চা খেলাম। তারপর বাজারে গেলাম। prôthôme āmrā chā khelām. tārpôr bājāre gelām. — "First we had tea. After that we went to the market."

প্রথমে, which you know, opens a story. তারপর (tārpôr), "after that, then", is new: তার, "of that", and পর, "after", the word inside পরে. তারপর starts each new step; পরে, "later", says the step came some time after.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: in the end

segments.text: শেষে (sheshe) is শেষ with -এ: "at the end, finally". It closes the story.
শেষে আমরা বাড়ি ফিরলাম। sheshe āmrā bāṛi phirlām. — "In the end we came back home."

segments.text: What opens a story? (প্রথমে.) What starts each next step? (তারপর.) What closes it? (শেষে.)
Before the new one: say "first", "after that" and "in the end". (prôthôme, tārpôr, sheshe.)
হঠাৎ — hôṭhāt — "suddenly".
আমি হাঁটছিলাম, হঠাৎ ঝড় এল। āmi hā̃ṭchhilām, hôṭhāt jhôṛ elô. — "I was walking, and suddenly a storm came."
A story goes প্রথমে, তারপর; হঠাৎ (hôṭhāt) is where it turns. It comes before the event that breaks into the scene.

হঠাৎ (hôṭhāt) is Sanskrit haṭhāt, "by force, forcibly", the ablative of haṭha, "force" (Monier-Williams). Monier-Williams also gives haṭhāt as "necessarily, inevitably". The Bengali sense, "suddenly", is not among the senses it lists, and the source does not say how the word came to it.

lessons.title: ৎ (t) — the letter at the end of হঠাৎ (hôṭhāt)
lessons.gloss: the letter ৎ — khanda ta, a t with no vowel after it, at the end of হঠাৎ

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
your eyes or your hands for the steps that ask you to read, point, write or gesture
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on, your eyes, for letter shapes on the page and your eyes or your hands for the steps that ask you to read, point, write or gesture. You can listen to everything else now. I will say so again when we reach them, but leave these sections until you have stopped: Warm-up, Script you'll notice: ৎ, Guided Practice and Wrap-up Recall.

segments.text: Before the new one: say হঠাৎ (hôṭhāt), "suddenly". Then read ত (tô) and the hasanta ্, the mark that takes a letter's vowel away.
ৎ — t, the khanda ta, "a piece of ta". It is a ত with no vowel after it. Where a word ends in that bare t, as হঠাৎ (hôṭhāt) does, Bengali often writes ৎ instead of ত with a hasanta.

In the print of this book, ৎ (t) has no headline. It is a round closed loop at the top, with a long slanting tail joined to the left side of the loop; the tail's lower end, at the bottom right, is a short upright foot.

blocks.title: Writing: ৎ — copy the printed shape

segments.text: Put your pen beside ৎ (t) and copy the shape you can see, slowly and large. Check the copy against the print: the round loop, the long tail, the short foot.

This book does not yet tell you where to start ৎ (t) or which way the pen goes. That is not written down here until it can be written down with a source. Copying the printed shape needs no such source, and it is how the shape becomes yours in the meantime.

lessons.title: (reading) (gôtô shônibār āmi didimār grāme gelām.) — a Saturday at Grandmother's village
lessons.romanization: gôtô shônibār āmi didimār grāme gelām.
lessons.gloss: a Saturday at Grandmother's village, in ninety-eight words, told with every past

needs: your eyes, to read the printed text yourself
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your eyes, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want your eyes, to read the printed text yourself. The questions are about what you read, so save the whole lesson for when you have stopped.

segments.text: Ninety-eight words, every one met before or explained after the story. The writer is Mira, telling of a Saturday at her grandmother's village.

গত শনিবার আমি দিদিমার গ্রামে গেলাম। প্রথমে বাসে স্টেশনে গেলাম। তারপর ট্রেনে চড়লাম। ট্রেনে আমি একটা বই পড়ছিলাম। হঠাৎ (hôṭhāt) ঝড় এল। ঠিক তখন ট্রেন একটা নদী পার হচ্ছিল। জানালার বাইরে আকাশ কালো ছিল, আর গাছগুলো কাঁপছিল। বিকেলে ট্রেন গ্রামের স্টেশনে থামল। তখন ঝড় ছিল না। আমি ট্রেন থেকে নেমে হেঁটে বাড়ি গেলাম। বাড়ি গিয়ে দেখলাম, দিদিমা রান্না করছিলেন। দাদু বারান্দায় বসে চা খাচ্ছিলেন। সন্ধ্যায় আমরা ভাত আর মাছ খেলাম। তারপর দিদিমা আমাকে একটা পুরনো গল্প বললেন। রাতে আবার ঝড় এল, কিন্তু আমরা ভিতরে ছিলাম। শেষে আমি তাড়াতাড়ি শুলাম। কাল সকালে আমি আবার শহরে ফিরব। দিনটা আমার ভালো লাগল।.

segments.text: New forms: দিদিমার, "Grandmother's", with the -র of আমার; শুলাম (shulām), শোয়া in the past, "I lay down to sleep"; দিনটা আমার ভালো লাগল, "the day felt good to me".
The scenes take -ছিল-; the events take the plain past, joined with -e forms and kept in order by প্রথমে, তারপর and শেষে. হঠাৎ (hôṭhāt) turns the story; ফিরব is the plan.
